set.st: In June 1901 Sheriff Martin Lins of Winona County and his deputies searched the big natural caverns in the bluffs near La Moille, thought to be a hideout of marauders. The largest opens 14 feet high into a chamber about 40 feet long, big enough to stable twenty horses, with a smaller cave off the side. That side cave had earlier been dug by a party searching for $8,000 in gold supposed to be hidden there; no find was ever announced. A Milwaukee paper's La Crosse dispatch of 7 June says the sheriff's party was after a gang of box-car thieves thought to hide in the cave west of La Crosse on the Minnesota side and found only tin cans; the $8,000 gold and the earlier digging party appear so far only in the St. Paul Globe account. Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself.
set.tovw: Lead grade C: a period paper reports the sheriff's search of the cave and an earlier dig for $8,000 in gold; the gold rests on that one account and no find was announced.

src: Milwaukee Daily News, 7 Jun 1901, p. 1, 'Searching a Cave for Box Car Thieves' (La Crosse, 7 Jun; Newspapers.com 1298936149)
